Compressor suction pressure is controlled from the upstream flow and motor variable frequency. Both compressors are equipped with VFD to adjust the rpm with pressure fluctuation. The suction & discharge motorized valve (MOV) are connected with the interlock during the start-up & emergency shutdown (Cause & Effect diagram will be prepared during the FEED study). Compressor discharge is further heated in a BF gas pre-heater (F01) from 315°F (Compressor discharge) to 767°F to meet the WGS Reactor required inlet temperature. NG-fired pre-heater consists of two convection banks with an induced draft fan & single radiant section to meet up the desired temperature. An online stack analyzer is there in natural gas (NG) fired heater to measure CO, CO , O , SOx, and NOx, which may 2 2 vary depending upon the variation of excess air used during fuel gas combustion. The inlet temperature of the reactor is controlled by the flow of NG a (as a heating medium) to the Feed gas preheater (F01). Low-pressure (LP) steam is injected to maintain the steam-to-dry gas ratio of 0.5. The system-generated LP steam from the WGS boiler is insufficient to meet this demand ratio. A separated LP steam control valve is placed to monitor the overall LP steam required for the system. 2 nos of the online analyzer are present at the inlet & outlet of the compressor for CO, CO and H to measure the reactor composition. Each reactor 2, 2 temperature is measured by different layers of thermowell due to the exothermicity of the process that may cause non-uniform heat distribution. The exothermic reactor inlet temperature is 608°F, and the outlet temperature is 839°F.
